Samir / team — I pulled the KV snapshot and the error snippets. Quick findings: 1) the KV prefixes show a recent growth pattern in prefix churn consistent with a caching cold-start across many simultaneous sessions, 2) decoded payloads include multiple truncated responses with a common decoder error: "KV-miss caused mid-token decode retry -> upstream 502 on the runtime process."

Hypothesis: a combination of aggressive concurrency from the customer side + insufficient KV warmup/caching for long contexts is producing a spike in cold loads and pushing the runtime into transient OOM/retry cycles on a subset of workers. That explains the mix of high p95 and intermittent 502s.

Immediate asks:
- Samir: can you confirm the spike pattern (concurrency and whether a new client version rolled out at ~03:00 PST)?
- Vivek: we should try a short-lived KV pre-warm (in-place) and increase the worker buffer thresholds, and temporarily route 15% of traffic to the fallback lower-capacity pool.

I will draft a tuning plan and attach a one-page PDF for execs.

Laura
Sr. Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [URGENT] Sharp p95 rise and intermittent 502s on our private cluster

Folks — quick technical mitigation we've validated in the staging replica:
1) KV pre-warm script (idempotent) to populate hot prefixes before traffic window (estimated 6–8 min run for Auratx dataset).
2) Incremental worker buffer increase from 256MB -> 384MB for decoding threads (reduces retry/oom tail).
3) Enable opportunistic batching with a 5ms coalescing window for long-context streams to reduce per-token overhead.

Proposed timeline (with Auratx approval):
- 00:00–00:10: run KV pre-warm (safe, read-only)
- 00:10–00:20: apply buffer increase and quick smoke test on 5% of workers
- 00:20–00:40: roll to 50% and monitor p95/error-rate; rollback plan in place

I will prepare a short runbook and a rollback procedure. Need Auratx SRE thumbs-up to run the pre-warm during their low traffic window (we recommend 02:00–03:00 PST).

Vivek
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
